Sir Nighteye was fatally wounded in the fight and, by canon default, died soon after; the hero world mourns him. Investigators keep what the house was building out of the news, but rumors spread among pros of bullets that can take a Quirk away for good, and agencies grow warier of yakuza houses and drug supply lines. The public hears only that a child was rescued, and nothing about who she is.\"]","L_p666":"[\"Unless the story has established otherwise, the heroes' raids on the Paranormal Liberation Front end in a victory nobody celebrates. Many of the Front's fighters were arrested, but Tomura Shigaraki and the League's leaders escaped with Gigantomachia, Jaku City was left in ruins, and during the battle mass breakouts from Tartarus and other prisons set many dangerous villains loose across Japan. Heroes fell or were maimed, Midnight and Crust among the dead by canon default, and many pros resign in the weeks after. Public trust in heroes collapses: people arm themselves, form neighborhood watches, protest outside agencies and crowd into shelters they believe are guarded. Students and pros alike are worn thin, and the news counts the missing every night.\"]","L_p667":"[\"Narrator only, true until the USJ attack: Tomura Shigaraki is planning his first big move, an attack on U.A. Kurogiri is gathering dozens of hired villains through brokers, paid in cash and told nothing about the target until the day.\"]","L_p668":"[\"Narrator only, true until the USJ attack: the detectives' office has a thin, growing file nobody has time for: over the last month several small-time crooks with fighting Quirks have stopped turning up at their usual haunts, and two were seen flashing new cash before they dropped out of sight. Tsukauchi has asked patrol officers to listen for a name.\"]","L_p669":"[\"Narrator only, true until the USJ attack: behind the arcade, a broker who never gives his name has been buying drinks for small-time crooks with fighting Quirks and handing out cash for paid work against heroes.
